Add website release notes with AI-powered generation pipeline (#3763)

Add website release notes with AI-powered generation pipeline (#3763)

SkiaSharp has had release notes on GitHub Releases since 2016, but
they were never surfaced on the website. Users had to navigate GitHub
to find what changed between versions. This PR adds a full release
notes section to the DocFX documentation site — 63 polished version
pages covering 10 years of releases — along with tooling to keep
them maintained automatically.

~~ release-notes skill ~~

New skill at `.agents/skills/release-notes/` that generates or
regenerates polished release notes for any version. Includes a
`generate-release-notes.py` script with four commands:

  * `--version X.Y.Z` — fetch raw GitHub release data
  * `--last N` — fetch the N most recent versions
  * `--unreleased` — find unreleased PRs via git commit ancestry
  * `--update-toc` — regenerate TOC.yml, index.md, and create
    the upcoming version file from SKIASHARP_VERSION

The unreleased command uses `git log {tag}..origin/main` instead of
date-based filtering, which correctly handles PRs merged before a
release date but after the release commit (the Skia m133 bump was
missed by the date approach). Baseline tag selection uses semver
comparison so a v3 hotfix tagged after a v4 preview doesn't shift
the diff window.

~~ update-release-notes agentic workflow ~~

`.github/workflows/update-release-notes.md` triggers on every push
to main. It runs the script to fetch unreleased PRs, reads
`TEMPLATE.md` as a style reference, and AI-polishes the raw list
into categorized notes with highlights, community attribution, and
platform tables. Self-bootstrapping: creates the version file and
TOC entry if the upcoming version doesn't exist yet.

~~ Template and formatting ~~

`TEMPLATE.md` is a real polished release notes page (3.119.2) with
inline HTML comments as formatting tips. One template serves all
three statuses — stable, preview-only, and upcoming — with the AI
adapting headers and sections based on version status.

~~ Website integration ~~

  * "Release Notes" tab in DocFX sidebar navigation
  * "Release Notes" link in landing page header nav
  * Release Notes card in homepage resources section
  * TOC groups versions by major.minor.x with "Obsolete Versions"
    node for 1.x and 2.x
  * Upcoming version reads from azure-templates-variables.yml and
    shows an (Upcoming) label

~~ Skill updates ~~

`release-publish` Step 7 now invokes the release-notes skill instead
of inlining formatting instructions. The skill generates files and
updates the TOC; release-publish handles the commit and push.

@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+---
+description: "Update the upcoming version's release notes when PRs merge to main."
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+    paths-ignore:
+      - "documentation/docfx/releases/*.md"
+      - ".github/**"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+  skip-bots: [github-actions, copilot, dependabot]
+concurrency:
+  group: update-release-notes
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+timeout-minutes: 10
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+tools:
+  bash: ["python3", "gh", "git", "cat", "grep"]
+  edit:
+network:
+  allowed:
+    - defaults
+safe-outputs:
+  create-pull-request:
+    title-prefix: "[docs] "
+    labels: [documentation]
+    draft: false
+---
+
+# Update Upcoming Release Notes
+
+When code merges to main, update the upcoming version's release notes page with a
+polished summary of all changes since the last release.
+
+## Step 1 — Set up
+
+Determine the upcoming version and ensure the file exists:
+
+```bash
+grep 'SKIASHARP_VERSION:' scripts/azure-templates-variables.yml
+```
+
+Extract the version number (e.g., `4.133.0`). Then ensure the version file and TOC exist:
+
+```bash
+python3 .agents/skills/release-notes/scripts/generate-release-notes.py --update-toc
+```
+
+This creates `documentation/docfx/releases/{version}.md` if missing and regenerates
+`TOC.yml` and `index.md`. Read the version file to see its current content.
+
+## Step 2 — Get raw change data
+
+Fetch the list of changes since the last release:
+
+```bash
+python3 .agents/skills/release-notes/scripts/generate-release-notes.py --unreleased --output /tmp/unreleased-raw.md
+```
+
+This uses git commit ancestry (not dates) to find all PRs on main that are not in the last
+release tag. Read `/tmp/unreleased-raw.md` to capture the raw content.
+
+## Step 3 — Read the template
+
+Read `documentation/docfx/releases/TEMPLATE.md`. This is a real example of a polished release
+notes page. Use it as the style reference — match its structure, tone, and formatting.
+
+The upcoming version adapts the template for unreleased status:
+- Use `> **Upcoming release** · In development · Not yet available on NuGet` as the header
+- Omit the Links section (no NuGet, no changelog, no API diff yet)
+- Omit Preview sections (no tagged previews yet)
+- Keep everything else: Highlights, Breaking Changes, New Features, Security, Bug Fixes,
+  Platform Support, Community Contributors
+
+## Step 4 — Write polished content
+
+Rewrite the raw PR list into polished release notes following the template:
+
+1. **Highlights** — 1-3 sentences. What's the story of this version? Lead with the biggest
+   changes. Mention community contributors by linked name.
+
+2. **Skia engine** — The version number encodes the Skia milestone (e.g., 4.**133**.0 = Skia m133).
+   Search for the merged bump PR: `gh pr list --repo mono/SkiaSharp --state merged --search "bump skia milestone {N}" --json number,title --limit 1`
+   If found, list it first under an **Engine** category. If the raw data already contains
+   a "Bump skia" PR, use that directly.
+
+3. **Categorize features** — Group by what they affect. Use sub-headers like:
+   Engine, GPU & Rendering, API Surface, Text & Fonts, Platform, Security, etc.
+   Each item: **bold title** — description. ❤️ [@contributor](https://github.com/contributor) ([#NNN](url))
+
+4. **Community contributors** — Anyone not `@mattleibow`. Mark with ❤️ inline AND list
+   in a Contributors table. **ALWAYS** link usernames: `[@user](https://github.com/user)`.
+   Never write bare `@user` anywhere.
+
+5. **Omit noise** — Skip version bumps, CI-only fixes, doc updates, workflow changes,
+   skill file edits. If many, mention as: "Plus several CI and documentation improvements."
+
+6. **Breaking changes** — If any PR has a `breaking` label or "BREAKING" in the title,
+   list under `### ⚠️ Breaking Changes` right after Highlights.
+
+7. **PR links** — Every item links to its PR: `([#NNN](url))`.
+
+If there are no user-facing changes, write: `*No user-facing changes yet.*`
+
+## Step 5 — Write the version file
+
+Use the `edit` tool to **replace the entire content** of `documentation/docfx/releases/{version}.md`
+with the polished release notes from Step 4.
+
+The file should follow the template structure exactly — title, blockquote header
+(`> **Upcoming release** · In development · Not yet available on NuGet`),
+then the polished sections (Highlights, Breaking Changes, New Features, etc.).
+
+No fence markers or placeholders needed — the workflow overwrites the whole file each run.

[release-notes] Reuse single PR and add effort metrics to workflow (#3782)

[release-notes] Reuse single PR and add effort metrics to workflow (#3782)

The "Update Upcoming Release Notes" agentic workflow was opening a new PR
on every push to main because the agent picked a unique branch name each
run. Meanwhile, the raw PR data lacked any signal about how much work each
change represented, making it harder for the formatting agent to prioritize
highlights.

~~ PR reuse ~~

Add Step 6 to the workflow instructions telling the agent to always use
`dev/upcoming-release-notes` as the branch name. The `create_pull_request`
safe-output detects an existing open PR on that branch and updates it in
place instead of creating a new one.

~~ Effort metrics ~~

Each PR line in the unreleased output now includes commit count and unique
working days — e.g. `(87 commits, 8 days)`. For PRs that link a companion
mono/skia PR in their body, the script also counts the skia-side effort by
the same authors, using `git log` on the `externals/skia` submodule with
a `base_sha..head_sha` range.

Author filtering ensures only commits by people who also contributed to the
SkiaSharp PR are counted, excluding the thousands of unrelated upstream
Skia committers in milestone merge PRs. The GitHub API silently truncates
PR commit lists at 100 entries, so git log is the only reliable approach
for large merge PRs (skia milestone bumps routinely have 4000+ commits).

Automate website release notes with branch-diffing script (#3787)

Automate website release notes with branch-diffing script

Replace manual release-notes generation (release-publish Step 7) with an
automated system. The update-release-notes agentic workflow triggers on
pushes to main, release/*, and v* tags, determines the branch, and
delegates to the release-notes skill.

The skill owns the entire pipeline:
1. generate-release-notes.py --branch diffs against the semver-sorted
   predecessor branch and writes raw PR data with YAML front-matter
   directly to documentation/docfx/releases/{version}.md
2. AI polishes the raw file using TEMPLATE.md
3. TOC.yml and index.md are regenerated automatically

Branch diff logic:
- main: diffs against latest release/{minor}.* branch
- release/X.Y.x: diffs against latest release/X.Y.* versioned branch
- release/X.Y.Z[-preview.N]: diffs against previous branch in semver order

The script emits three-state status (unreleased/preview/stable) so the
AI selects the correct header format. Includes safety checks: fatal on
git fetch failure, warning+abort when >50% of PR fetches fail, refusal
to diff entire history when no release branches exist.

Also adds polished release notes for 3.119.0-3.119.4 and 4.147.0, and
removes stale 4.133.0.md (version was never released).

commits.message:
Make release notes script fully git-based with cumulative rollup (#3815)

Make release notes script fully git-based with cumulative rollup (#3815)

The release notes script relied on `gh` CLI for PR metadata and GitHub
API calls for release status and effort metrics. This broke in agentic
workflow containers where `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set but `gh auth login`
hasn't run.

Rewrite the script to derive everything from git history — PR numbers,
authors, titles, dates, commit counts, and working days all come from
`git log`. Release status uses `git tag -l`. Skia companion PRs are
detected by scanning commit messages for `mono/skia#NNN`. Zero API
calls, zero tokens needed.

~~ Cumulative rollup for first-in-minor branches ~~

The old diff logic used `merge-base` against the immediate predecessor,
producing 0 PRs for first-in-minor branches like
`release/4.147.0-preview.1` (just a fork of main with version bumps).

New `find_previous_stable_base()` walks back across minors to find the
correct base — for 4.147.0-preview.1 that's `release/3.119.4-preview.1`,
giving the expected 63-PR cumulative rollup.

~~ Side-effect scoping and file independence ~~

When a versioned branch is pushed, the script regenerates unreleased
files whose diff range may have changed. Two fixes:

  * Only regenerate main's unreleased when the trigger branch is in the
    same minor. A 3.119.x push no longer overwrites 4.147.0-unreleased.
  * Script prints a "Files to polish" list; skill instructs agents to
    polish every listed file using only that file's own raw PR data.

Also removes the stale agentics-maintenance workflow (506 lines) and
`gh` CLI from workflow tools.

fix: preserve branch name in release notes workflow to reuse PRs (#3822)

The create-pull-request safe output adds a random salt suffix to branch
names by default (preserve-branch-name defaults to false). This caused
every workflow run to create a new branch and a new PR instead of
updating the existing one for the same version.

name (dev/release-notes-{VERSION}) is used exactly, so subsequent runs
push to the same branch and update the same PR.

fix: add recreate-ref to release notes workflow for branch reuse (#3836)

When preserve-branch-name is true and the branch already exists from a
previous run, the patch fails because the stale branch has diverged from
main. Setting recreate-ref: true force-deletes the stale remote ref and
recreates it from the agent's local HEAD (force-push semantics), keeping
the existing PR open with updated content.

Requires gh-aw v0.71.4+ (pre-release) which adds the recreate-ref field.

Fix release notes workflow to always checkout main (#4059)

[Workflows] Fix release notes workflow to always checkout main (#4059)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4053

When a push to a release branch (e.g. `release/4.147.0-preview.3`) triggered the
`update-release-notes` agentic workflow, the agent checked out that release branch.
Since the generated PR targets `main`, release-branch-specific files like
`PREVIEW_LABEL` in `scripts/azure-templates-variables.yml` bled into the diff,
producing a broken PR (#4053 was closed for this reason).

A secondary issue: both release-branch and main-branch triggers used the same PR
branch name (`dev/release-notes-{VERSION}`), so a main push shortly after a release
push would force-push over the first PR's branch, closing it.

Fix both problems:

- Add `git checkout main` + `git fetch origin` in Step 2 so the working tree is
  always based on main regardless of the triggering ref. The release-notes script
  only uses `origin/` remote refs for git history queries, so this is safe.
- Use distinct PR branch names per trigger type:
  `dev/release-notes-{VERSION}-released` for release branches,
  `dev/release-notes-{VERSION}-unreleased` for main.

commits.message:
Unify API changelog + release-notes versioning via shared versions.json (#4171)

Unify API changelog + release-notes versioning via shared versions.json (#4171)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4171

The two documentation-automation systems — API changelogs (Cake targets) and
website release notes (Python script) — each auto-detected version
relationships on their own, and each got abandoned-preview releases wrong. Some
versions ship previews then get dropped (e.g. 4.147.* never went stable; its
work rolled up into 4.148). Both systems must still *generate* output for the
dead version but must *skip* it when picking a baseline for later versions, so
4.148 compares back to 3.119.4 rather than to the abandoned 4.147. The bespoke
per-system "magic" handled this inconsistently and produced wrong baselines and
mislabelled banners.

Replace that magic with one shared override config, scripts/versions.json, read
by both systems. Each version simply compares to its predecessor; versions.json

[docs] Unify API-diff + release-notes into one agentic workflow (#4184)

The API changelogs and the website release notes were two disconnected
systems. Each had its own version-comparison logic and lived in a different
place (changelogs/ vs documentation/docfx/releases/), driven by a separate
workflow. They drifted: a line could get release notes but no matching API
diff, or be diffed against the wrong baseline, because the Cake side and the
Python side each guessed at "what is the previous version" independently.

The 4.147/4.148 cycle made the cost concrete. 4.147 shipped preview-only and
never went stable, and the old auto-detection handled that supersession case
inconsistently across the two engines. Fixing it once, shared, was the
trigger for this change.

This unifies both systems onto one versioning model, one engine pair, and one
workflow that opens a single PR, with all output living in the in-site
documentation/docfx/releases/ tree so changelogs and notes stay consistent.

Versioning model:
  * scripts/infra/docs/versions.json is now the single source of truth for
    both engines. It is override-only and family-bucketed (skiasharp /
    harfbuzzsharp): the default baseline for a line is the previous emitted
    line, and an entry is added only to declare a non-default compare_to or
    to mark a line superseded. The old per-engine auto-detection is gone.
  * Superseded preview lines still emit pages: 4.147 and 4.148 both diff
    against the last stable 3.119.4.

HarfBuzzSharp peer family:
  * HarfBuzzSharp versions independently of SkiaSharp, so it now has its own
    hub pages and API-diff folders, linked to the SkiaSharp line it ships
    with via a generated co-release map, and grouped by major.minor.x in the
    TOC. Both engines and the spec treat it as a first-class peer rather than
    a special case.

Workflow and layout:
  * A deterministic Prepare host step (full SDK + network) runs Cake API-diff
    then Python release-notes and emits a clean "files to polish" list; the AI
    Polish step rewrites prose only, copying script-owned content verbatim. A
    no-op run produces no PR.
  * The API-changelog engine was extracted out of docs.cake into the skill's
    api-diff.cake plus shared helpers; docs.cake now owns only the mdoc/XML
    framework-docs pipeline, which was verified to still run end to end.
  * The standalone api-diff.yml workflow and the top-level changelogs/ tree
    are removed; CI callers point at the in-site releases/ tree.
  * documentation/dev/release-notes-and-changelogs.md is the durable spec for
    the versioning model, orchestration, on-disk layout, both engines, and
    editing rules.

This PR also deletes the newest generated lines (SkiaSharp 4.147.0/4.148.0/
4.150.0 and their HarfBuzz peers 14.2.0 and 8.3.1.6) on purpose, so the
post-merge scheduled workflow regenerates them and opens its own PR — an
end-to-end dogfood of the automation.

[infra] Run release-notes Prepare in its own disk-managed job (#4193)

[infra] Run release-notes Prepare in its own disk-managed job (#4193)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/27767832525
Fixes: #4191

The first post-merge auto-run of the unified release-notes + API-changelog
workflow (#4184) failed with `No space left on device` ~11.5 minutes in, opened
no regeneration PR, and auto-filed failure issue #4191. The deterministic Prepare
phase (`generate.sh` -> Cake `docs-api-diff-past` + Python `--all`) ran as
pre-agent host steps *inside* the agent job, sharing its disk and clock. The
historical API diff downloads every published package of both the SkiaSharp and
HarfBuzz families (prereleases included); after the HarfBuzz peer family roughly
doubled the download set, Mono.ApiTools.NuGetDiff's package cache exhausted the
~14 GB hosted-runner disk and took the whole job down. The failure was also
invisible until the job died, because the script hid all Cake/Python progress in
a temp log to keep stdout clean for the "Files to polish" list.

Move Prepare into a dedicated `prepare` job so the heavy, network-bound
generation can neither starve nor hide from the agent. The job gets its own
runner, a 120-minute timeout, and a free-disk-space step that drops unused
preinstalled toolchains before the NuGet diff. It runs the generators verbose, so
all progress (and any disk/timeout failure) is visible in the job log. It then
hands its result to the agent as a workflow artifact: a binary git patch of every
working-tree change (the releases tree, the co-release-map sidecar, the author
cache, any pruning) plus the files-to-polish list. The agent job declares
`needs: prepare` (added automatically by the gh-aw compiler), resets to a clean
origin/main, replays the patch with `git apply --3way`, and polishes prose only --
it no longer runs cake/python/git-write itself, and python3 is dropped from its
tool allow-list.

While here, settle the polish-list handoff on one simple contract. The Python
engine now ALWAYS writes the "Files to polish" list to a file -- a plain list,
one repo-relative path per line, no decoration -- defaulting to the gitignored
output/files-to-polish.txt; an empty file still means "nothing changed", which is
what suppresses the no-op PR. There is no stdout-scraping path and no "====" /
"Files to polish:" summary block anymore: everything (progress and the raw list)
streams to STDERR, and the list lives only in the file. The automated workflow
restores that list to the very same output/files-to-polish.txt the agent reads,
so the skill's Polish phase is byte-for-byte identical whether it was triggered by
the workflow or run by hand. The release-notes SKILL.md was trimmed to match: it
no longer describes jobs, runners, artifacts, or /tmp paths -- only "manual = run
the script then read output/files-to-polish.txt, automated = skip the script and
read the same file".

  * generate-release-notes.py: write_polish_list() always writes the file (and
    echoes the raw paths to STDERR); --polish-list overrides only the location;
    the decorated stdout summary blocks are gone.
  * generate.sh: run verbose (no temp-log redirect); forward --polish-list.
  * update-release-notes.md/.lock.yml: define jobs.prepare with disk management +
    artifact upload; the agent restores the list to output/files-to-polish.txt.
  * SKILL.md: drop the workflow plumbing; always point at output/files-to-polish.txt.
  * release-notes-and-changelogs.md (the spec) updated first: standalone job,
    verbose output, always-a-file polish list, artifact handoff, plus a new §7.2
    invariant so this cannot silently regress.

A workflow_dispatch smoke test on the branch (run 27773439793) confirmed the job
graph fires -- pre_activation -> activation -> prepare, with the free-disk and
clean-main steps passing. The scripts themselves only run for real once merged,
because both jobs reset their tree to origin/main before generating; a failed
post-merge run auto-files an issue, so a regression stays visible.

Make doc generation reproducible and Linux-only; unify "API diff" terminology (#4200)

Make doc generation reproducible and Linux-only; unify "API diff" terminology (#4200)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4200
Companion: mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs#147 (must merge after this)
Supersedes the drifted releases/ baseline committed in #4184.

The repo generates its release documentation through three independent paths,
and two of them produced different output depending on the build host or the
local NuGet-cache warmth. That non-determinism made the doc-bot's regenerated
output "wobble" between runs and was nearly impossible to reproduce locally,
so a reviewer could never tell an intended doc change from host noise. This
PR makes all three paths deterministic, gives them one shared set of entry
points that behave identically locally / in CI / in Docker (Linux), unifies
the "changelog" vs "release notes" terminology onto "API diff", and commits a
freshly regenerated, byte-reproducible baseline.

~~ Path 1 — API diffs: deterministic and correct ~~

Self-dependency resolution used a filesystem glob over the warm package cache,
so the chosen baseline depended on what happened to be unpacked locally. Simply
deleting the glob restored determinism but regressed correctness: ApiInfo must
resolve SkiaSharp.dll to see that the two infrastructure interfaces SKObject
implements (ISKReferenceCounted, ISKSkipObjectRegistration) are internal and
collapse to the public System.IDisposable; without it those internal names
leaked into the public diff (8 files). The fix stages each self-dependency
per-diff at the exact version pinned in that package's own .nuspec
(StageSelfDepsFromNuspecAsync) — contemporaneous, host- and cache-independent.
Two more leaks are closed at the source: auto-generated resource designers
(Android aapt R.*, Uno/WinUI GlobalStaticResources) are excluded via
IgnoreMemberRegex, and the TFM selector now ranks candidates (newest plain
.NET → netstandard → portable) instead of taking filesystem-enumeration order,
so SkiaSharp is diffed from net10.0 and the choice is stable.

~~ Path 3 — mdoc API docs: ref/ over lib/, on Mono/Linux ~~

mdoc was fed the lib/ implementation assemblies, which still carry ABI-compat
members marked [Obsolete(error: true)] (e.g. by-value SetMatrix(SKMatrix)).
mdoc's comparer ignores the by-ref marker and sorts unstably, and because it
runs in merge mode the pair swapped places every run — a 2-cycle with no fixed
point. The C# compiler strips error-obsolete members from ref/, so docs.cake
now prefers the ref/ surface (lib/ fallback) and invokes mdoc via Mono so the
path runs on Linux.

~~ One home, one set of entry points ~~

The API-diff and release-notes engines moved out of the release-notes skill and
scripts/infra/shared into scripts/infra/docs alongside docs.cake (git renames).
local / CI / Docker now all call the same git-free shell entry points
(generate-{api-diffs,release-notes,api-docs}.sh), and a reproducible Linux
image (scripts/infra/docs/docker) matches CI exactly.

~~ CI, terminology, and docs ~~

A new workflow_dispatch source_branch input (default: main, every existing
trigger byte-identical) lets a manual run validate a feature branch's doc-gen
pipeline before merge, mirroring the docs repo's skiasharp_branch input. The
"changelog" vocabulary — which collided with "release notes" and GitHub's own
"Full Changelog" compare links — is unified onto "API diff" across scripts,
Cake identifiers, log paths, the dev spec, and the recompiled workflow lock;
GitHub's literal compare links are intentionally left as-is. The developer
docs that describe the system are also added/restructured for readability — a
new docs-overview.md map and a re-laid-out release-notes-and-api-diffs.md spec
(both gain a TOC); the relayout is information-preserving and keeps the spec's
numbered headings byte-identical, since ~120 code comments reference them.

~~ Baseline ~~

The regenerated releases/ tree replaces the drifted #4184 output; a full
regeneration in the Linux Docker harness reproduced the committed API-diff
baseline byte-for-byte. The 4.148.0/ and harfbuzzsharp/14.2.0/ API-diff trees
are deliberately left deleted to prove CI's post-merge self-heal recreates
exactly them (the PR description records the expected 33-file recreate set).

[docs] Release-notes: main-only daily workflow + GitHub Release teaser playbook (#4207)

[docs] Release-notes: main-only daily workflow + GitHub Release teaser playbook (#4207)

Two related changes to how SkiaSharp release notes are produced — one for the
website release-notes/API-diff automation, one for the GitHub Release body.
Skill, workflow, and docs only; no product code.

~~ Harden the website release-notes workflow ~~

The unified "Update Release Notes & API Diffs" workflow was opening duplicate
PRs and occasionally diffing months of history. Two root causes:

  * The agent created a branch but never committed, so gh-aw's patch fallback
    diffed the whole branch (the original E003 failure). It now commits on the
    agent branch *before* gh-aw opens the PR.
  * `release/*` and `v*` tag triggers ran a *stale per-branch copy* of the
    workflow: a push/tag event runs the file living on that ref, not on main.
    That produced the duplicate dev/release-notes-* PRs (#4172, #4208, #4210,
    #4213) alongside the unified bot/release-notes PR.

The Prepare generators already walk every release/* ref and read v* tags
themselves, so one run from main covers all branches. Drop the release/** and
v* triggers, keep push:[main] + workflow_dispatch, and move the safety-net cron
from weekly to daily. Prepare now does `git fetch --tags --force` so a freshly
pushed stable tag flips that version's page to stable on the next run, and it
emits a has_changes flag that gates the agent job — an unchanged daily run
skips the agent and the PR deterministically instead of trusting the LLM to
notice an empty work list.

Because tags no longer auto-trigger, the release-publish skill gains a post-tag
"Refresh Website Release Notes & API Diffs" step (Step 5) that dispatches the
workflow from main so the site updates immediately after a stable release
rather than waiting up to a day for the cron.

~~ GitHub Release teaser playbook ~~

Maintainers found the flat 100+ line auto-generated PR list "too heavy and hard
to find things." Replace the old per-PR emoji-annotation step with a short,
scannable customer teaser, with GitHub's full PR list folded beneath it
(release-publish Step 7). Rename references/release-notes.md to
references/github-release-teaser.md and rewrite it as a self-contained playbook:

  * Classify breaking-first: ⚠️ Breaking → ✨ What's New → 🐛 Fixes →
    📦 Dependency Updates (empty sections omitted). Breaking leads because that
    is what consumers most need to see. The new 🐛 Fixes section surfaces
    consumer-visible bug fixes the old prompt was folding — confirmed by an A/B
    test where two models both missed the same PRs.
  * Treat the Skia milestone bump as a headline ✨ feature, not a dependency;
    routine [skia-sync] engine merges stay folded.
  * Never advertise security: native-library bumps read neutrally as
    "Updated <dep> to <version>"; upstream CVE text stays verbatim only in the
    fold.
  * Credit every contributor inline (by @author (#NNNN)) plus a roll-up of the
    unique community handles.
  * Use a 2-line header: a neutral subtitle, then NuGet · Release notes · Full
    changelog, where the notes link uses the base X.Y.Z line and the compare URL
    moves up out of the fold so it appears once.

The doc is the single source of truth (full rules + a worked example); SKILL.md
Step 7 keeps only a short prompt that defers to it, and Step 5 is trimmed of
generator implementation detail so the runbook stays instruction-focused.

Validated by re-applying the playbook — via agents, reading only each release's
raw auto-generated log — to all six live GitHub Releases (v3.119.4 through
v4.150.0-preview.1.1) and grading each result against the hard rules.

Follow-up: the stale per-version workflow files still living on release/4.148.x
are removed in #4217.

the `Docs - *` set was grouped; everything else was scattered. This PR

    docs): Deploy, Go Live!, PR Staging - Cleanup, PR Staging - Sweep Stale

    Submodule, Release Notes & API Diffs, Agentic Data, Issue Triage, Samples

keeps its exact name — GitHub special-cases it).

and our tooling reference workflows *by name*, so those references are
updated in lockstep to avoid silently breaking the chained automation:

release-notes: manual notes sidecar + AI-summarized breaking changes (#4334)

Two tied capabilities for the spec-driven release-notes system, plus a
refinement to how the API-diff / breaking companions are surfaced. This
closes a real gap: behavioral breaking changes (same signature, different
runtime behavior — e.g. `new SKFont()` now carries an empty typeface,
`SKPaint().Typeface` returns Default instead of null) never appear in a
signature diff, so today they reach the notes through no channel at all.

~~ Manual additions sidecar (`<stem>.notes.md`) ~~

A maintainer-authored, freeform-Markdown sidecar co-located with a
version's hub page. It is never machine-overwritten: the generator hashes
its bytes into the page content key (`notes:`) and the Polish AI reads and
weaves it into the prose, so it survives `--branch` / `--all` regeneration
and re-polish. This is the durable home for behavioral breaks and for any
point a maintainer simply wants brought out — not all of it is "breaking".
The file is docfx-excluded and discovery-guarded, so it is never treated
as a version page or emitted into the TOC.

~~ AI-summarized breaking changes (companion model) ~~

The page's raw-data block now references companion files by path + hash
rather than embedding them, and the Polish AI opens and summarizes them
into a `## ⚠️ Breaking Changes` section:

  * API diff → a single `index.md` entry: the version folder's landing
    page that links every per-assembly diff and flags the breaking ones.
  * API breaking diff → one `- breaking:` line per broken assembly, folded
    into one order-stable combined `breaking:` hash. Paths keep their
    package-folder prefix so identically-named files (e.g.
    `SkiaSharp.Views.Windows.breaking.md` under both `Uno.WinUI/` and
    `WinUI/`) stay distinct. A major release like 3.116.0 enumerates all
    twelve.

~~ Behavior and rollout ~~

The content key (`_is_content_unchanged`) now folds in the `notes:` and
`breaking:` hashes, so a companion-only edit re-polishes exactly that page
and everything stays idempotent. On the first `--all` run, the 25 pages
that predate the feature but carry a breaking diff gain the `breaking:`
manifest + section as a one-time backfill; unaffected pages are skipped.

(run 28677098312): Prepare + Polish ran green off this branch's scripts +
skill, re-polished exactly the 25 breaking-bearing pages, and wrote correct
`## Breaking Changes` prose for 3.116.0 (12 companions) and 4.148.0 (1).

Spec-first order, matching the repo rule: spec (§3.7 sidecar, §4.7
companions) → generator → docfx exclusion → TEMPLATE.md → SKILL.md →
workflow (Polish pinned to a stronger model for companion summarization).

[release-notes] Rebuild generation as a deterministic pipeline (#4389)

[release-notes] Rebuild generation as a deterministic pipeline (#4389)

Replaces the old "AI polishes a whole .md page" generator — which kept dropping
headings, bare @handles, contributors, and links — with a deterministic JSON core
plus a thin prose surface. Scripts now own every byte of page structure; the agent
writes only prose strings the renderer validates, so those classes of breakage are
structurally impossible. The page is exactly `render(data.json, prose.json)`.

~~ The pipeline: two commands, one flag set ~~

    prepare.sh  →  (agent writes prose.json per page)  →  render.sh
     (network)            (release-notes skill)             (offline)

prepare.sh runs Cake `docs-api-diff` (API-diff tree + co-release-map.json), then
release-notes-data.py (per-page _sources/<version>.data.json facts), then
release-notes-index.py (_sources/index.json: Chrome schedule + live-head set).
render.sh runs release-notes-render.py --all: re-renders every page, prunes stale
-unreleased heads, and rebuilds TOC.yml + index.md from committed JSON, offline.
Both take only --force / --min-version / --max-version; everything is incremental,
so an unforced run skips work whose output already exists (a shipped API diff never
changes) and there is no "notes-only" mode.

~~ Engines co-located; the skill is a thin surface ~~

All three doc engines live together under scripts/infra/docs/ (the Cake api-diff +
mdoc engines and the renamed release-notes-data/-index/-render.py, next to their
shared versions.json). The skill keeps only SKILL.md, samples/, and the two thin
entrypoints prepare.sh + render.sh, which redirect to the engine. This keeps the
skill simple while the real code sits with the other doc engines — until the Cake
api-diff engine can be retired and folded in.

~~ Committed inputs under _sources/ ~~

Every page input is committed beside the page: _sources/<version>.data.json (facts),
.prose.json (the agent's slots), optional .notes.md (manual additions sidecar),
co-release-map.json (the Cake→python HarfBuzz hand-off), index.json, and the
pr-authors.json author cache. data.json is the timestamp-free whole-file
change-detection key, and the committed JSON lets render.sh reproduce every page
byte-for-byte with no network.

~~ HarfBuzzSharp folded into each SkiaSharp page ~~

There is no separate HarfBuzz family (34 pages removed). HB ships inside each
SkiaSharp release, so it renders as a "## HarfBuzzSharp X.Y.Z" section on the
SkiaSharp page with its own API-diff link, derived from the co-release map.

~~ Incremental, scoped Cake api-diff; legacy gate removed ~~

The single docs-api-diff target skips a line whose folder already has an index.md
unless forced, scopes by version range, and writes a merged {skia_line: hb_line}
co-release-map so scoped runs keep prior entries. The old build-pipeline api-diff
gate (its build.cake task + the api_diff stage in azure-templates-stages-test.yml)
is removed as superseded by the skill + workflow.

~~ Preview keys made unique (core-qualified) ~~

Preview/RC keys in data.json — the handle prose maps summaries onto — are now
core-qualified as <core>-<stage><num> (e.g. 4.148.0-rc1, 3.118.0-p1, 1.53.2-gpu1).
This fixes real collisions a review caught on old pages: nonstandard 2016 trains
(Svg 1 / Gpu 1 both keyed m1) and cross-line roll-ups (two Preview 1s both p1)
previously shared one summary. release-notes-data.py now raises on any duplicate
key, and the renderer validates one summary per preview, so a collision can never
silently ship.

~~ Consolidation ~~

  * generate-release-notes.py → release-notes-data.py; generate-release-notes.sh,
    generate.sh, build-data.sh → replaced by prepare.sh + render.sh.
  * generate-api-diffs.sh folded into prepare.sh (it was release-notes-only).
  * pr-authors.json moved into releases/_sources/.
  * references/TEMPLATE.md, grouping.md, review-checklist.md folded into SKILL.md —
    the renderer is the checklist, so there is one instruction file, not four.
  * The workflow prompt was de-duplicated to defer to the skill for the "how",
    keeping only the CI-specific deltas.

~~ Fixes found while validating ~~

  * Cadence double-prepare: a scoped local regen used to need two prepare passes
    because cadence_milestones() read the in-flight Chrome milestones from the
    rendered .md (which build-index runs before). Now derived from the
    _sources/*.data.json written earlier in Prepare, so a single prepare → render
    works.
  * API-diff banner on prerelease-only lines now links both the SkiaSharp and
    HarfBuzzSharp diffs (committing the line's <version>/ folder lets
    release-notes-data.py attach the SkiaSharp link).

~~ Validation ~~

All 1.x–4.x pages were regenerated with this pipeline (default Copilot model for
polish; an A/B run matched the previously-pinned model). Multiple full CI runs are
green (Prepare + agent + detection; safe_outputs fails pre-merge by design because a
feature branch's patch touches protected paths). Incrementality was verified
end-to-end: deleting 4.151.0 and running a no-force `min 4.147.0` CI job regenerated
exactly 4.151.0 plus 4.150.1-unreleased (a real new PR) and skipped 4.147/4.148.

Spec-first: documentation/dev/release-notes-and-api-diffs.md is the behaviour spec;
docs-overview.md, writing-docs.md, and AGENTS.md are synced to the final pipeline.

[docs] Publish the 4.148.0 v4 breaking notes: fix sidecar path + re-trigger (#4420)

[docs] Publish the 4.148.0 v4 breaking notes: fix sidecar path + re-trigger (#4420)

Context: #3734 (umbrella for the v4 / Skia m132–m147 breaking changes)

A maintainer hand-authored a "manual additions" sidecar documenting the six
v4 breaking changes that an API signature diff cannot detect — behavioral
and interop-struct changes — so they could be published on the 4.148.0
release-notes page. The file was committed to the releases root
(documentation/docfx/releases/4.148.0.notes.md) instead of the canonical
_sources/ location the generator actually reads.

The generator's load_notes_sidecar() only looks for
releases/_sources/<version>.notes.md, so at the root the file was invisible:
4.148.0.data.json got no notes-sidecar candidate and the six breaks never
made it onto 4.148.0.md's "## Breaking Changes" section. Nothing warned about
it, so the omission went unnoticed.

Two changes:

  * Relocate the sidecar (git mv, content verbatim) to
    documentation/docfx/releases/_sources/4.148.0.notes.md so the generator
    consumes it. The regenerated data.json / prose.json / 4.148.0.md are
    produced by the release-notes pipeline, not hand-edited here.

  * Fix the reason a standalone sidecar edit publishes nothing: the
    update-release-notes push trigger ignored the entire
    documentation/docfx/releases/** tree (to avoid re-running on its own
    generated output), which also swallowed the human-editable *.notes.md
    sidecars. Switch from paths-ignore to negated `paths` so the generated
    pages/inputs stay ignored but any *.notes.md change re-triggers a run:

        paths:
          - "**"
          - "!documentation/docfx/releases/**"
          - "documentation/docfx/releases/**/*.notes.md"

    The engine already handles the rest once triggered — the sidecar's sha256
    is folded into data.json, so an edited/added sidecar flips the
    change-detection key, rewrites data.json, discards stale prose.json, and
    forces a re-polish. update-release-notes.lock.yml was recompiled with
    `gh aw compile update-release-notes` (v0.71.5); only the frontmatter hash,
    the trigger block, and content-derived heredoc delimiters change.

The six breaks this restores to the page: #3735 (new SKFont() empty typeface),
#3736 (new SKPaint().Typeface → Default), #3737 (FromFamilyName("missing") →
Default on Android), #3738 (SKTypeface.Default via the font manager), #3740
(SKStream.Move(long) throws + [Obsolete]), #3741 (Vulkan
GRVkBackendContextNative field removals + GrVkYcbcrConversionInfo layout).

Follow-up for a maintainer to decide: once these render on 4.148.0.md, the
tracking issues #3734/#3735/#3736/#3737/#3738/#3740/#3741 (currently
milestoned to 4.151.0-preview.2) can likely be closed or re-milestoned — they
document m147 breaks that shipped in 4.147/4.148, not 4.151.
